key_insight: The paper shows that the linear Poisson source for wall-pressure fluctuations stays inner-scaled and Reynolds-number independent, so the observed logarithmic growth in wall-pressure variance must come from the nonlinear source.
engineering_relevance: This clarifies which turbulence mechanism controls high-Re wall-pressure loads, improving modeling of boundary-layer noise, vibration, and wall-pressure prediction in aerodynamic design.
method: Analyzed simultaneous velocity and velocity-gradient hot-wire data from Zimmermann et al. (2019).
Compared source-term scaling in both a zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layer and a high-Reynolds-number pipe flow.
Checked inner-scaling collapse of linear-source factors and the wall-distance decay of inertial-layer gradient variance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports collapse of the inner-scaled factors across Reynolds number and inverse wall-distance decay of the relevant inertial-layer velocity-gradient variance up to friction Reynolds numbers of order 10^4.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on indirect source-term inference from hot-wire measurements, so probe resolution and the assumptions behind the Poisson decomposition may limit how directly the scaling transfers to other flows.
paper_title: An Inner-Scaled Linear Contribution to Wall-Pressure Variance at High Reynolds Number
